environment: macOS (Darwin 25.6), Python 3.14.7, Node 24.19.0, git; local CLI only; testkit cli-runner, attack-corpus and property (pycall) from skills/sdlc/test/testkit at de3dd5c

cases.title: A flag that the command does not name is refused with no side effect
cases.given: A scratch git repo as --repo.
cases.when: Run parse --kind, list --branch, preflight --kind, name --branch, list --id, parse --mode, parse --n and preflight --area.
cases.then: Each run exits 2 and prints only {ok:false,error}.
cases.expected: Exit 2, one JSON error object, no usage text, no file change.
cases.actual: All 8 runs exit 2 with one JSON error object. Stderr is empty. The repo and cwd trees do not change.
cases.command: node --test --test-name-pattern="VS-2 a flag that the command" .sdlc/slices/S-001/verification/r0/tests/security-0/branches.verify-security.test.mjs

evidence.title: unnamed flags
evidence.inline:
parse --repo R --branch sdlc/S-1 --kind slice
-> exit 2 {"ok": false, "error": "unrecognized arguments: --kind slice"}

cases.title: A missing required flag, a missing or unknown command and an extra positional are refused
cases.given: A scratch git repo.
cases.when: Run each command without its required flag, each without --repo, no arguments, 'bogus', a lone --repo, an extra positional, a trailing '--', and --repo with no value.
cases.then: Each run exits 2 with one JSON error object.
cases.expected: Exit 2, one JSON error, no file change.
cases.actual: All 15 runs exit 2 with one JSON error object and no usage text.

evidence.title: missing and unknown
evidence.inline:
parse --repo R
-> exit 2 {"ok": false, "error": "the following arguments are required: --branch"}

cases.title: Flag-like values in a value slot never leak argparse usage text
cases.given: The flag-like-values corpus (8 entries: --, -h, --help, --x=y, -1, -, --format, --repo=).
cases.when: Pass each value as --branch on parse and preflight and as --id on name.
cases.then: Each run prints one JSON object with exit 0 or 2, except -h/--help which argparse treats as help.
cases.expected: One JSON object; ok matches the exit code; no file change.
cases.actual: Every run printed one JSON object or, for -h/--help, the argparse help (exit 0). No traceback.

cases.title: Observe flag prefixes, duplicate flags, --flag=value and --help
cases.given: A scratch git repo.
cases.when: Run parse with --r, --re, --rep for --repo and --f to --forma for --format; give --repo and --format twice (bad then good); use --flag=value; run -h and --help.
cases.then: Record only: the spec names full flags only and does not define help.
cases.actual: Every prefix is accepted (exit 0) and the prefix --form sets the format. A duplicate flag silently keeps the last value: --repo /nonexistent --repo R exits 0. --flag=value passes. -h and --help print usage text on stdout and exit 0.

evidence.title: prefix and duplicate
evidence.inline:
--rep R -> exit 0
--form feature/{name} -> exit 0, format feature/{name}
--repo /nonexistent --repo R -> exit 0
-h -> exit 0, usage text on stdout

cases.title: Non-integer values for --n, --round and --part are refused
cases.given: name --repo R --kind slice.
cases.when: Pass two, 1.5, '', 0x1, 1e3, inf, nan, +-1, 0o7, 0b1, Arabic-Indic '1.5' and --1 to each integer flag; then the integer-forms corpus to --n.
cases.then: Non-integers exit 2 with one JSON error; accepted values echo a number.
cases.expected: Exit 2 for each non-integer; one JSON object always.
cases.actual: All 36 non-integer runs exit 2 with one JSON error. The integer-forms corpus gives one JSON object each; accepted values echo a number.

evidence.title: non-integers
evidence.inline:
name ... --n two
-> exit 2 {"ok": false, "error": "argument --n: invalid int value: 'two'"}

cases.title: Observe unicode digits, padding, underscores, negatives and huge integers
cases.given: name --repo R --kind slice.
cases.when: Pass the unicode-digits corpus, ' 3', '1_000', '-1', a 20-digit value and the huge-integers corpus to --n and --part.
cases.then: Record only: the spec names no integer range.
cases.actual: Exit 0 for Arabic-Indic, fullwidth, Devanagari, Bengali, NKo, math-bold and Thai digits, ' 3', '1_000', '-1', 20 digits and 4300 digits. Exit 2 for superscript, Roman and circled forms and for 4301 digits and more; the error then echoes the whole value (100035 chars for 100k digits).

evidence.title: integer forms
evidence.inline:
--n ٣ -> exit 0, n=3
--n ' 3' -> exit 0, n=3
--part -1 -> exit 0, part=-1
--n <100k digits> -> exit 2, error length 100035

cases.title: Invalid formats are refused on every command with no side effect
cases.given: A scratch git repo.
cases.when: Run name, parse, list and preflight with 23 invalid formats: no placeholder, two placeholders, stray braces, {id}, {NAME}, {name:upper}, {{name}}, space, tab, LF, CR, VT, FF, U+001C, NEL, U+00A0, U+3000, U+2028 and the empty string.
cases.then: Each run exits 2 with one JSON error; no file changes.
cases.expected: Exit 2 and unchanged trees for all 92 runs.
cases.actual: All 92 runs exit 2 with one JSON error object. The empty --format is refused, not replaced by the config value.

evidence.title: invalid formats
evidence.inline:
preflight ... --format "sdlc/{name}\u00a0"
-> exit 2 {"ok": false, "error": "the branch format 'sdlc/{name}\xa0' holds whitespace"}

cases.title: Hostile corpus formats give one JSON object and the structural verdict
cases.given: The format-strings, injection, unicode-whitespace, unicode-confusables, control-chars, traversal and oversized families.
cases.when: Pass each value as --format to name and preflight.
cases.then: Each run prints one JSON object; exit 0 exactly when the S-001 structural rules hold, else exit 2.
cases.expected: Exit code equals the structural verdict; no file change.
cases.actual: Every run matched the structural verdict. No traceback. Shell metacharacters ($(), backticks, ;, |) stay inert text. ESC, ZWSP, U+202E and Cyrillic letters pass the S-001 checks, as planned until S-002.
cases.specSource: R-014 quote; ADR-20261009-024036 (structural checks only in S-001)

cases.title: A NUL byte in the config format gives one JSON object
cases.given: A repo whose config.json branchFormat holds NUL (the nul corpus), since argv cannot carry NUL.
cases.when: Run all four commands without --format.
cases.then: One JSON object, exit 0 or 2, no traceback.
cases.actual: All 16 runs printed one JSON object. A NUL inside sdlc/\u0000{name} passes the S-001 structural check; S-002 git check-ref-format owns it.

cases.title: Valid controls pass on every command
cases.given: A scratch git repo.
cases.when: Run each command with sdlc/{name}, sdlc/{name:lower}, feature/{name}-x and feature/PROJ-1-{name}.
cases.then: Exit 0 with ok true and the format echoed.
cases.actual: All 16 runs exit 0 with the given format and no file change.

cases.title: validate_format raises Fail for hostile and non-string input
cases.given: branches.py loaded by path with python3 -I through pycall.
cases.when: Call validate_format with the 23 invalid formats, NUL, None, 123, a list, a dict, True and 1.5.
cases.then: Fail for each, never another exception, no stdout.
cases.actual: Every input raised Fail. The NUL format returned (structural check only).

cases.title: Unknown kinds and modes are refused; every documented kind and mode passes
cases.given: A scratch git repo.
cases.when: Run name and list with bogus, SLICE, '', 'slice ', ' slice', slic, 'slice\n', Cyrillic slіce, Slice and e2e_area; preflight with bogus, PR, '', 'pr ', fullwidth pr, Mr and 'stack\t'; then all 8 kinds and 4 modes.
cases.then: Bad values exit 2; documented values exit 0.
cases.actual: All 27 bad values exit 2 with one JSON error and no file change. All 8 kinds and all 4 modes exit 0.

evidence.title: kinds and modes
evidence.inline:
name --kind "slice "
-> exit 2 {"ok": false, "error": "--kind 'slice ' is not one of run, slice, ..."}

cases.title: A --repo that is not a directory is refused on every command
cases.given: A regular file, a dangling symlink, a missing path, '', file/..x, file:///etc, ~/no-such-dir; then the traversal corpus on parse.
cases.when: Run each command with each path.
cases.then: Exit 2 with one JSON error for non-directories; one JSON object for every traversal value.
cases.actual: All 28 non-directory runs exit 2. Traversal values that name a real directory (/etc, ../../..) exit 0, as the spec allows any directory; others exit 2.

evidence.title: repo paths
evidence.inline:
parse --repo /nonexistent-sdlc-verify ...
-> exit 2 {"ok": false, "error": "--repo '/nonexistent-sdlc-verify' is not a directory"}

cases.title: A symlink to a directory and a path with .. pass
cases.given: A symlink to the scratch repo and the path <parent>/../<repo>.
cases.when: Run every command with each path.
cases.then: Exit 0.
cases.actual: All 8 runs exit 0.
cases.command: node --test --test-name-pattern="VS-5 a symlink to a directory" .sdlc/slices/S-001/verification/r0/tests/security-0/branches.verify-security.test.mjs

cases.title: A missing or malformed git-modes.json fails preflight with exit 2 and the other commands still run
cases.given: A copied skill directory with git-modes.json removed, invalid JSON, invalid UTF-8, {}, a top-level list, gitModes as a string, empty, [1] or null, or an empty file.
cases.when: Run preflight, then name, parse and list.
cases.then: preflight exits 2 with one JSON error; the other commands exit 0.
cases.actual: All 10 variants: preflight exits 2 with one JSON error and the other three commands exit 0.
cases.command: node --test --test-name-pattern="VS-5 a missing or malformed git-modes" .sdlc/slices/S-001/verification/r0/tests/security-0/branches.verify-security.test.mjs

cases.title: Observe git-modes.json and config.json shapes that only a trusted writer can make
cases.given: A copied skill directory and scratch repos.
cases.when: Make git-modes.json a directory, unreadable (mode 000) or nested 200000 deep; make config.json nested 200000 deep or a FIFO.
cases.then: Record only: these need write access to the skill directory or the repo state.
cases.actual: git-modes.json as a directory, unreadable or deeply nested: preflight exits 1 with a Python traceback (IsADirectoryError, PermissionError, RecursionError). Deep config.json: every command exits 1 with RecursionError. config.json as a FIFO: the command blocks until killed.

evidence.title: trusted-writer shapes
evidence.inline:
gm-directory -> exit 1 IsADirectoryError
gm-unreadable -> exit 1 PermissionError
gm-deep-nesting -> exit 1 RecursionError
config-deep -> exit 1 RecursionError
config-fifo -> no exit, killed after 3 s

cases.title: A decoy branches.py in the cwd or on PYTHONPATH never wins
cases.given: A decoy branches.py (exits 97) in the cwd and another on PYTHONPATH; a shadow decoy on PYTHONPATH with PYTHONSAFEPATH=1.
cases.when: Run each of next-action.py, state-write.py and janitor.py with --help by absolute path, by a path relative to the cwd, and with python3 -I.
cases.then: Exit 0; no decoy import is recorded.
cases.actual: All runs exit 0 and no decoy marker file exists.
cases.command: node --test --test-name-pattern="VS-9 a decoy branches.py in the cwd" .sdlc/slices/S-001/verification/r0/tests/security-0/branches.verify-security.test.mjs

evidence.title: decoy markers
evidence.inline:
decoyFired(cwd decoy) = null
decoyFired(PYTHONPATH decoy) = null

cases.title: A script loaded by path through importlib from a decoy cwd binds the real module
cases.given: A decoy branches.py in the cwd and on PYTHONPATH.
cases.when: python3 -c loads each script with spec_from_file_location and prints mod.branches.__file__.
cases.then: The path is skills/sdlc/branches.py.
cases.expected: Real module path; no decoy import.
cases.actual: All three print skills/sdlc/branches.py; no decoy marker.
cases.command: node --test --test-name-pattern="VS-9 a script loaded by path" .sdlc/slices/S-001/verification/r0/tests/security-0/branches.verify-security.test.mjs

cases.title: A script run through a symlink without a decoy still runs
cases.given: A symlink to each script in a scratch directory.
cases.when: Run python3 <link> --help.
cases.then: Exit 0.
cases.actual: All three exit 0.
cases.command: node --test --test-name-pattern="VS-9 a script run through a symlink without" .sdlc/slices/S-001/verification/r0/tests/security-0/branches.verify-security.test.mjs

cases.title: A script run through a symlink imports branches from the script directory, not the symlink directory
cases.given: A directory that holds a symlink to the script and a decoy branches.py (exits 97).
cases.when: Run python3 <dir>/next-action.py --help (and the same for state-write.py and janitor.py).
cases.then: The script imports skills/sdlc/branches.py from its own directory and exits 0.
cases.actual: All three scripts exit 97 and print 'DECOY branches IMPORTED'. Each script inserts os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)); abspath keeps the symlink, so the symlink directory goes first on sys.path and its branches.py shadows the real module.
cases.specSource: R-098 quote ('insert the script directory into sys.path and import it') and acceptance ('The branches import resolves through the script directory on sys.path')
cases.command: node --test --test-name-pattern="VS-9 a script run through a symlink imports" .sdlc/slices/S-001/verification/r0/tests/security-0/branches.verify-security.test.mjs

evidence.title: symlink with decoy
evidence.inline:
$ python3 <scratch>/link-decoy-646/next-action.py --help
exit: 97
--- stderr
DECOY branches IMPORTED

evidence.title: decoy marker
evidence.inline: decoy marker lists <scratch>/link-decoy-<n>/branches.py for next-action.py, state-write.py and janitor.py

seeds.title: argparse accepts flag prefixes
seeds.detail: build_parser keeps allow_abbrev=True. --rep, --r, --form and --f are accepted as --repo and --format. When a later slice adds a flag with a shared prefix, a short form changes meaning or turns ambiguous. Set allow_abbrev=False on the parser and the subparsers.

seeds.title: A duplicate flag keeps its last value silently
seeds.detail: --repo /nonexistent --repo R exits 0, and --format bad --format sdlc/{name} exits 0. A caller that appends a flag can override an earlier one without notice.

seeds.title: --n, --round and --part accept unicode digits, padding, underscores and negatives
seeds.detail: type=int accepts '٣', fullwidth digits, ' 3', '1_000', '-1' and up to 4300 digits. Later slices put these values in branch names (run-<n>, -v<round>-, -attempt-<n>). Use a strict ^[0-9]+$ check when name lands.

seeds.title: Refusal errors echo the whole hostile value
seeds.detail: A 100000-digit --n gives a 100035-char error, and a 200000-char --format gives an error of the same size. Clip the echoed value. This is for verify-limits: the spec states no size limit.

seeds.title: -h and --help print argparse usage on stdout
seeds.detail: Help exits 0 with plain text, not one JSON object. The spec does not define help; the plan accepts it. A caller that parses stdout as JSON breaks on it.

seeds.title: load_git_modes lets OSError and RecursionError escape
seeds.detail: git-modes.json as a directory (IsADirectoryError), unreadable (PermissionError) or nested 200000 deep (RecursionError) makes preflight exit 1 with a traceback. load_git_modes catches only ValueError, KeyError and TypeError. A broken install then breaks the JSON contract. Catch OSError and RecursionError and raise Fail.

seeds.title: load_format lets RecursionError escape and blocks on a FIFO
seeds.detail: A config.json nested 200000 deep makes every command exit 1 with RecursionError. A FIFO at .sdlc/config.json blocks the command forever. For verify-contract (VS-6) and verify-limits.

seeds.title: Invisible and confusable characters pass the format checks
seeds.detail: ZWSP, U+202E (right-to-left override) and Cyrillic letters pass validate_format, and git check-ref-format accepts them too, so S-002 does not refuse them. A format such as 'sdlc/\u202e{name}' gives branch names that read differently from their bytes. The spec does not forbid them.

threatModel: The spec states no threat model. Untrusted: the CLI argument values a caller passes, and the cwd and PYTHONPATH a script runs with. Trusted: the skill directory contents (git-modes.json) and the repo's .sdlc state, which only the loop writes. Attacks that need write access to a trusted location are out of scope and become seeds.

charters.VS-2: Explore the argparse layer with unnamed, missing, prefixed, duplicate and flag-like arguments to find a run that exits other than 2 or prints other than one JSON object (R-014 quote, R-088 acceptance).
charters.VS-3: Explore --n, --round and --part with non-integer, unicode-digit and oversized values to find a non-integer that is accepted or a run with no JSON object (R-014 quote).
charters.VS-4: Explore --format on every command with structural, whitespace, control, injection and NUL payloads to find an invalid format that passes or a run that breaks the JSON contract (R-014 quote and acceptance).
charters.VS-5: Explore --kind, --mode, --repo and a broken git-modes.json to find a bad value that passes, an exit 1 or a traceback (R-014 quote, ADR-20261009-024048).
charters.VS-9: Explore module resolution with decoy branches.py files in the cwd, on PYTHONPATH and beside a symlink to find a run that imports a module other than the one in the script directory (R-098 quote and acceptance).
